document: CEP Visualize Owner Direct Requirements Ledger v1.3 — Interaction/Customization Hardened
source_note_preserved: هناك ملاحظة مهمة: all four views must be freely editable. كل node/item/thing في Tree/Path/Graph/Canvas يجب أن يكون قابلًا للتحرير والتعديل المهني؛ Canvas ليس وحده الـinteractive/editable view. Tree/Path/Graph يجب أن تصبح بيئات تحرير كاملة، بمستوى Canvas أو أفضل بحسب semantics الخاصة بها. كذلك Canvas الحالي من ناحية التصميم ما زال بدائيًا/طفوليًا ويحتاج تحسينًا واسعًا في visual design, functionality, responsiveness, experience, branding وغيرها.

Tree/Path/Graph يجب أن تصبح بيئات تحرير كاملة، بمستوى Canvas أو أفضل بحسب semantics الخاصة بها. كذلك Canvas الحالي من ناحية التصميم ما زال بدائيًا/طفوليًا ويحتاج تحسينًا واسعًا في visual design, functionality, responsiveness, experience, branding وغيرها.
requirements.requirement: Tree, Path, Graph, and Canvas are all full professional editing environments. No view may be reduced to a mostly-read-only visualization merely because Canvas is the free-spatial view.
requirements.interpretation: Freely editable means every user-owned, semantically editable object/property/relationship/projection in that view has a direct or equivalently efficient editing path. It does NOT mean every view gets identical spatial freedom.
requirements.authority_boundary: Canonical relation creation/edit/delete and canonical Tree containment commit remain AUTHORITY_GATED unless direct authority opens them. Working/draft/presentation edits must remain fully available without pretending to commit canonical truth.
requirements.acceptance: Each view must pass a capability matrix covering select/multi-select, inspect, rename/edit label, add draft, remove/hide projection where admissible, move/reorder/layout where semantically valid, relation/link draft where admissible, Notes, Undo/Redo, keyboard parity, pointer parity, responsive reachability, state synchronization, and truthful gated states.

requirements.requirement: Tree must be a full hierarchy editing workspace, not a static hierarchy viewer.
requirements.semantic_constraint: Tree remains hierarchy-constrained. No arbitrary free x/y positioning. Canonical containment commit is authority-gated; staged hierarchy proposals are fully editable and reversible.
requirements.acceptance: Every visible task-relevant Tree item exposes an editing route with keyboard equivalent for essential actions; no pointer-only structural edit.

requirements.requirement: Path must be a full ordered/progression editing workspace, not a decorative journey diagram.
required_capabilities: stage/order/progression adjustment as working presentation/proposal state
requirements.semantic_constraint: Path preserves ordered/progression semantics. It must not become a free Canvas clone; canonical relationship commit remains authority-gated.
requirements.acceptance: Every task-relevant Path node/edge/stage control is inspectable and editable through pointer and keyboard paths where essential.

requirements.requirement: Graph must be a full semantic relationship editing workspace, not only an exploration viewer.
requirements.semantic_constraint: Graph edits relationship/projection working state according to authority. Canonical relation mutation remains gated unless explicitly opened.
requirements.acceptance: Nodes and task-relevant edges are keyboard focusable/selectable; all essential editing workflows have non-pointer routes.

requirements.requirement: Canvas remains fully editable and must not regress while the other views are raised to parity.
requirements.semantic_constraint: Representation edits never silently mutate canonical object identity/relationship stores.
requirements.acceptance: Canvas preserves all proven working functionality while converging to one owner per state/command/history path.

requirements.requirement: Canvas visual/product quality must be materially reconstructed from its current primitive/toy-like presentation into a premium CEP spatial workstation.
required_improvements: clear type differentiation without color-only meaning
better spatial depth and background/grid treatment
requirements.reference_law: Use Canvas reference for useful design grammar, not literal cloning. Functionality/accessibility/responsiveness may add components absent from the image.
requirements.acceptance: At 1440 and ~1024 the Canvas must read as a mature branded CEP product surface, not a prototype/demo, while retaining all editing functionality.

requirements.requirement: Create and enforce a cross-view editability capability matrix so shared editing concepts are not implemented only in Canvas.
requirements.acceptance: No shared capability is absent from Tree/Path/Graph merely because an implementation already exists in Canvas; NOT_APPLICABLE requires explicit semantic reason.

requirements.requirement: Editability must survive responsive and accessibility states; narrow/zoom modes may reorganize controls but may not silently turn a view read-only.
requirements.acceptance: At 1440, ~1024, 840/720 stress and actual 200% browser zoom, essential edit/inspect/undo/context operations remain reachable for all four views, with same-owner responsive panels and no body-level horizontal overflow.

requirements.owner_note: Owner requires highly organized, intelligently grouped toolbars/context actions with progressive disclosure; one professional Notes system with fast node-anchored editing and same-instance Sticky Note escalation; a professional Visualize editor with multi-route accessibility and familiar mouse/keyboard interaction; blank left-drag marquee, restored pan navigation through alternate gestures, wheel scroll/pan and Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zoom; strong CENTER/work focus; and extreme customization so guides, legends, panels, toolbars and small chrome can be moved/hidden/shown/configured rather than forced permanently visible.
requirements.requirement: All Visualize tools/actions must use a coherent, low-clutter, progressively disclosed command architecture rather than being scattered across permanent toolbars and panels.
prohibited: duplicated command homes with separate state owners
permanent guide/tool islands that crowd CENTER
requirements.acceptance: At 1440 and ~1024, primary commands remain immediately reachable without horizontal tool-scroll; secondary/advanced commands are grouped by intent; right-click, contextual toolbar, persistent toolbar, inspector and command palette route to the same semantic command owner; no duplicated side-effect implementations.

requirements.requirement: Tool families with multiple variants/options must use the interaction pattern best suited to that family, not one generic list/dropdown for everything.
requirements.acceptance: Writer documents each family and chooses among split-button, segmented mode group, remembered-last-tool flyout, popover grid, nested submenu, swatch/slider popover, or overflow collection; each group has keyboard navigation, accessible naming, state indication and responsive fallback.

requirements.requirement: Right-click on a node/item/edge/stage/representation opens a context-sensitive action hub whose content is capability-driven by view + object + selection, not a generic duplicated menu.
requirements.acceptance: Context menu exposes high-value object/selection actions, grouped with progressive disclosure; disabled/unavailable actions explain why; keyboard Shift+F10/Menu key reaches the same command definitions; menu closes via command, explicit close where large, outside click and Escape with deterministic focus return.

requirements.requirement: Visualize must have one professional Notes system that supports immediate object-anchored editing and deep Sticky Note editing without separate note engines or duplicate note instances.
requirements.acceptance: note.new on an object creates/opens one NoteWorkingState bound read-only to source identity; quick invocation opens a compact anchored editor near the object; Open as Sticky/Pin promotes the SAME instance to movable/resizable StickyNoteWindow; Context Notes lens lists/opens the same instances; reopening never duplicates; Undo/recovery and Bidi/editor/clipboard semantics remain shared; durable persistence remains AUTHORITY_GATED.

requirements.requirement: Visualize editing quality must meet the same professional interaction standard as the Library editor: direct editability, low friction, reversible operations, precise selection, alignment/arrangement, predictable menus, rich shortcuts, and no toy/demo feel.
requirements.acceptance: Every admitted editable property/action has direct pointer and keyboard-equivalent access or an equally efficient alternative; selection/primary/focus are distinct; align/distribute/layout/nudge/lock/copy/note/edit-label/duplicate/remove/history behave through one transaction/command model; no silent no-op; focus/caret/object identity survives rerender where semantically applicable.

requirements.requirement: Provide a familiar, conflict-safe default mouse navigation grammar while allowing remapping/custom profiles.
external_ergonomic_precedent: Miro: selection-field drag; right/Space/middle-assisted pan options; configurable mouse/trackpad navigation
FigJam: Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zoom and configurable wheel zoom
requirements.acceptance: Default profile: blank LEFT drag in Select mode = marquee; object LEFT drag = move/admitted drag; RIGHT click = context actions; Space+LEFT drag = temporary pan; middle-button drag = pan when supported; wheel = vertical pan/scroll; Shift+wheel = horizontal pan; Ctrl/Cmd+wheel = pointer-centered zoom; fit/zoom remain keyboard accessible. Ctrl/Cmd+LEFT drag pan may be offered as an OPTIONAL remap, not default, because Ctrl/Cmd+click commonly participates in multi-selection.

requirements.requirement: Essential Visualize actions must be accessible through multiple coherent routes without creating multiple state owners.
requirements.accessibility_invariant: Multiple entry routes converge on one semantic command owner.
requirements.acceptance: Critical operations have keyboard routes and are discoverable in shortcut help/Command Palette; object traversal/select, multi-select, context menu, edit, nudge/reorder, pan, zoom, fit, focus/right inspector, Notes, Undo/Redo and transient close/return are keyboard-operable. Pointer-only essential steps are prohibited. Shortcut conflicts are detected and surfaced in Settings.

requirements.requirement: Workspace chrome should be user-customizable at very fine granularity: visibility, docking/position, order, density and behavior should be preferences wherever technically/semantically safe.
requirements.invariant: Customization may hide/reposition presentation chrome but must not eliminate the last accessible route to Settings/Reset/Command Palette, required error/status/safety/authority disclosure, or mandatory accessibility recovery.
requirements.acceptance: User can show/hide or auto-show applicable guides, legends, minimap, grid/ruler, state strip, selection frame, note badges, tool groups, TOP_BANNER, LEFT/RIGHT/BOTTOM, contextual helpers and nonessential chrome; applicable toolbars can be reordered, pinned/unpinned and docked to allowed workspace zones or floated; preferred state persists and responsive effective overrides restore it later.

requirements.requirement: Provide reusable workspace customization profiles plus per-view overrides instead of forcing one fixed layout.
requirements.persistence: PreferenceStore versioned snapshot; production backend remains a replaceable StorageAdapter seam.
requirements.acceptance: At minimum Default, Focus, Editing, Exploration, Presentation and Custom profiles exist as presentation-preference bundles; user may choose global shared preferences plus Tree/Path/Graph/Canvas overrides; switching profile is reversible and preserves working/canonical data.

requirements.requirement: Mouse/keyboard bindings for Visualize navigation and tools should be user-configurable with safe defaults and conflict detection.
requirements.default_profile: Professional CEP Visualize default based on familiar editor/whiteboard conventions.
requirements.acceptance: Settings exposes binding profile, searchable command bindings, remap/reset, conflict warnings and import/export through PreferenceStore; browser/OS-reserved combinations are identified truthfully; remapping changes entry routes only, not command semantics/state owners.

requirements.requirement: The surface must remain unmistakably centered on the actual visual work: CENTER dominates; tools support the work rather than visually compete with it.
requirements.quality: No scattered-tool demo feel; no mandatory permanent legend that competes with the work.
requirements.acceptance: At all target widths, overlays/menus/toolbars avoid permanently consuming excessive CENTER space; contextual tools appear near relevance and disappear/compact when idle; Focus Mode can reduce nonessential chrome losslessly; the active view, selection and current editing intention remain immediately understandable.

requirements.requirement: Reference-derived guides/legends/relationship keys/rulers must never become permanently mandatory merely because they appear in a reference image.
requirements.reference_law: Reference image provides intent/grammar only; it cannot override customization/functionality/accessibility requirements.
requirements.acceptance: Every nonessential guide/legend/ruler has SHOW/HIDE/AUTO (or equivalent) preference; state persists; keyboard/Settings route exists; hiding it does not hide the underlying semantic meaning from accessibility—object/edge labels and inspector semantics remain available.

requirements.requirement: Extreme customization must include deterministic recovery so experimentation cannot strand the user.
requirements.acceptance: Always provide Reset current view, Reset workspace layout, Reset input bindings, and Restore default visibility; import/export is versioned; unsupported/old preference keys migrate or fall back safely; responsive temporary overrides never overwrite preferred customization.

requirements.requirement: Toolbars themselves are customizable presentation surfaces rather than fixed immutable chrome.
external_ergonomic_precedent: Miro allows reorder/add/remove of creation toolbar tools
Figma groups related toolbar tools and exposes actions/search for broader command access
requirements.acceptance: Eligible tools can be reordered, pinned/unpinned, grouped, hidden, restored and assigned to allowed toolbar zones; frequently used last-tool state may be remembered; responsive layout collapses lower-priority groups into overflow without losing commands; personalization is per-user preference, not canonical workspace data.
